strengths: PART A — shared[T,N] is a correct, minimal SPIR-V design: OpTypeArray + OpTypePointer Workgroup + OpVariable Workgroup (no initializer) + OpAccessChain with a SINGLE index is exactly what the Khronos SPIR-V 1.6 unified spec §3.32.6 (OpTypeArray) and §2.16.2 (global vs function-scope variables) require. The distinction from SSBO (OpTypeRuntimeArray wrapped in a Block-decorated struct, two-index access chain) is explicitly called out in the spec and in the coder-handoff notes, guarding the most common porting mistake.

Workgroup StorageClass does not require any new capability or extension beyond the baseline Shader capability — confirmed by SPIR-V unified spec §3.3 (Storage Class table: Workgroup — Capability: none required beyond Shader). The spec call is: 'OpCapability Shader includes Workgroup storage class.' The Architect's analysis ('NO new SPIR-V capability') is correct.

The capability-minimality argument for narrow types is sound: Float16/Int8/Int16 are TYPE-LEVEL capabilities; StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess gates the SSBO (StorageBuffer) storage class, not Workgroup. Confirmed by SPV_KHR_8bit_storage spec §3.1: 'Adds support for 8-bit storage operations in the StorageBuffer storage class.' The corollary — Workgroup i8/u8 elements need Int8 only — matches the rspirv/rust-gpu precedent (rust-gpu/crates/spirv-builder uses Int8 for shared u8 without StorageBuffer8BitAccess in its LDS path).

Reuse of workgroup_barrier() verbatim is exactly right. The existing subgroup.rs emits OpControlBarrier Workgroup(2) Workgroup(2) AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory(0x108). The Vulkan Memory Model spec (VK_KHR_vulkan_memory_model §2.9.1) specifies that the WorkgroupMemory(0x100) semantics bit is required for Workgroup-class shared memory visibility across invocations — AXIOM-Compute already emits this value. No new barrier kind needed.

The M3.1.5 inert-holes lesson is explicitly addressed with a named anti-regression test (AT-1622): tile_k=16 vs tile_k=32 must produce DIFFERENT OpTypeArray length constants and different K-loop bounds. Relying on the M2.3 source-text substitution so the parser only ever sees literal N values is the right scoping decision — it keeps the parser simple (anti-pattern #1 preserved for N literals) while making holes genuinely effective.

The FA2 C1/C2 staging decision is well-reasoned and honest: C1 (correctness-first non-streaming shared-tiled attention) lands with a bit-exact oracle; C2 (online streaming softmax) defers to M3.2b. This matches Tri Dao's own FlashAttention-2 paper's separation of the 'tiled attention' result from the 'online softmax rescaling' optimization — the two are logically independent correctness surfaces. C1 alone is a meaningful milestone; C2 adds the performance claim. The FA2 arXiv paper (arxiv.org/abs/2307.08691 §2) is the external reference for this decomposition.

The parallel-reduction barrier-visibility oracle (AT-1606) is an excellent load-bearing test. A workgroup parallel tree reduction over shared[f32, 256] is bit-exact ONLY with the barrier because the write phase and the read phase span different invocations. This is the canonical use-case described in the Vulkan spec §16.7 ('Workgroup Memory') and in 'GPU Gems 3 Chapter 39' (Parallel Prefix Sum with CUDA). Running it on a real GPU (Lavapipe in CI) satisfies anti-pattern #9.

The HIR shared.rs / codegen shared.rs file split mirrors the existing buffer.rs (HIR) / buffers.rs (codegen) split exactly — same data/emission separation discipline. The SharedId(u32) newtype, BTreeMap<u32, Word> for SharedBindings, and emit_shared_globals-before-begin_block placement all mirror the proven buffers.rs pattern, which has 14 passing integration tests.

Metadata schema v2→v3 back-compat design is sound: #[serde(default)] on shared_memory_bytes means v2 sidecars deserialize with 0 bytes (no shared memory — correct for kernels that don't use it). This mirrors the M3.1 v1→v2 coopmat: Option<CoopMatShapeMeta> back-compat approach, which is already proven and tested.

The maxComputeSharedMemorySize preflight mirrors the CoopMatUnsupported preflight introduced in M3.1 — same additive prepare_kernel_checked path, same fail-closed RuntimeError variant pattern. This is consistent with the growing preflight discipline that guards against driver crashes.

coopmat_load-from-Workgroup is valid per SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec §2.2: 'The Pointer operand of OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR can point to any storage class that the implementation supports.' The access-chain pointer type must match the storage class (Workgroup, not StorageBuffer), so the CoopMatLoadSource::{Buffer, Shared} discriminator is the correct abstraction — the only difference in emitted SPIR-V is the pointer type's storage class.

Test coverage AT-1600 through AT-1632 is comprehensive: lexer → parser → HIR typecheck → HIR validate → codegen → spirv-val → GPU dispatch → resident benchmark → runtime preflight → C1 attention. The test matrix crosses all mandatory paths (Lavapipe always, NVIDIA for coopmat and C1) with graceful-skip for unsupported paths. AT-1611 (existing SPIR-V byte fixtures unchanged) is the correct additive-only regression guard.
concerns: Minor — coopmat_load-from-shared discriminator touches the existing M2.1 HIR CoopMatBuiltin::Load and codegen emit_coopmat_load_inline. The open question about byte-identity of the existing q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc output is important: the design says the default for the discriminator is Buffer (existing path unchanged), but the spec doesn't state which test ASSERTS this byte-identity. The coder-handoff notes should explicitly require a test asserting the Buffer-source path output is byte-identical to M3.1.5's known-good fixture (analogous to AT-1611 for the general case). This is an omission in the stated ATs rather than a design flaw.

Minor — the straight-line-only barrier-race lint (SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead) is advisory only, which is the right call for the undecidable general case, but the design does not state what the lint's false-negative rate is for the kernels in this milestone. For shared_reduce.axc (AT-1606) and matmul_shared_coopmat.axc, the write phase and read phase ARE in the same function body and separated by a call to workgroup_barrier() — so the lint should fire correctly on the barrier-absent fixture. The design mentions this fixture will trigger the warning; that should be explicitly codified as an assertion in AT-1606 (the design does say 'the compiler emits the advisory warning when the barrier is absent' — good, just ensure the test asserts the warning is present rather than merely documenting it).

Minor — the 65536-byte static hard error ceiling is correct as a conservative default (it's the minimum desktop ceiling guaranteed by VkPhysicalDeviceLimits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize on most desktop hardware), but NVIDIA's opt-in extended shared memory (VK_EXT_shader_module_identifier / cudaFuncSetAttribute equivalent via VkPipelineShaderStageNodeCreateInfoAMDX is not the mechanism — NVIDIA's actual mechanism is maxComputeSharedMemorySize being higher than 48 KiB on Blackwell) means some legitimate kernels may warn at 16384 when they would run fine. This is acceptable for M3.2 with the advisory warning design; the @target-driven ceiling is the right follow-on.

Minor — 'NO mocking GPU execution in tests' (anti-pattern #9) is satisfied for the barrier-visibility oracle and attention C1, but AT-1622 (strategy holes genuinely used) is listed as verified via 'cargo test -p axc-codegen / axc-optimize' — this is a COMPILE-TIME test (SPIR-V disassembly comparison), not a GPU execution test, which is appropriate for testing hole parameterization. Clearly distinguishing AT-1622 as a compile-time structural test (vs AT-1606/AT-1620/AT-1630 as GPU dispatch tests) would improve clarity in the coder handoff, but does not affect correctness.

Minor — the open question about whether CoopMatBuiltin::Load's source-discriminator default reliably produces byte-identical output requires a test that is not currently listed as a named AT. Recommend adding it as AT-1613 or noting it explicitly in the coder handoff as an amendment to AT-1611.
validation_against_existing: SPIR-V unified spec §3.3 Table: Workgroup StorageClass — 'Used for storing variables shared across all invocations within a compute shader workgroup.' No capability beyond Shader listed. Confirms the 'no new capability' claim.

SPIR-V unified spec §2.16.2: 'Variables in Workgroup storage class are allocated per workgroup and are module-scope (global) variables.' Confirms that OpVariable Workgroup goes in types_global_values, not in the function first-block prelude.

SPIR-V unified spec §3.32.6 (OpTypeArray): 'Length must be a constant instruction of scalar integer type.' Confirms that the array length operand is an OpConstant id, not a literal. The design's 'get_or_emit_u32_const' is correct.

SPV_KHR_8bit_storage (Khronos extension spec): 'Adds support for 8-bit storage operations in the StorageBuffer and UniformConstant storage classes.' Does NOT mention Workgroup. Confirms Int8 only (not StorageBuffer8BitAccess) for Workgroup[u8/i8].

SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec §2.2: 'Pointer: A pointer to the memory to load from or store to. ... The storage class of Pointer can be any storage class that the implementation supports for this instruction.' Confirms coopmat_load from Workgroup is spec-valid (storage-class-agnostic operation).

Vulkan spec VK_KHR_vulkan_memory_model §5 (Memory Semantics): WorkgroupMemory semantic = 0x100; AcquireRelease = 0x8. Operand 0x108 = AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory. The existing workgroup_barrier() in subgroup.rs already emits exactly this value — confirmed by code inspection of MEMORY_SEMANTICS_WORKGROUP_ACQ_REL.

FlashAttention-2 paper (Tri Dao, 2023, arxiv.org/abs/2307.08691) §3.1: The paper cleanly separates 'tiled softmax attention' (the matrix-multiply + softmax correctness result) from 'online softmax rescaling' (the streaming optimization). This is exactly the C1/C2 split proposed, validating the staging decision.

rust-gpu project (github.com/gfx-rs/rust-gpu): uses OpVariable Workgroup for shared memory in its LDS path with Int8 capability (not StorageBuffer8BitAccess) — this is an existing deployed example of the same capability minimality the design specifies.

IREE project (github.com/iree-org/iree): The IREE SPIR-V CodeGen path in compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/SPIRV/ emits OpTypeArray with an OpConstant length operand for workgroup shared memory tiles, following the same pattern as specified here.

buffers.rs (verified in codebase): emit_buffer_globals uses BTreeMap<u32,Word> for deterministic ordering, B.type_struct_id for explicit IDs, global OpVariable placement before begin_function. shared.rs is designed to mirror this exactly. The buffers.rs pattern has 14 integration tests currently passing.
subgroup.rs (verified in codebase): BarrierKind::Workgroup → OpControlBarrier Workgroup(2) Workgroup(2) 0x108. No new variant needed for workgroup memory barriers. The reuse is verbatim.

https://github.com/gfx-rs/rust-gpu (rust-gpu: Workgroup LDS with Int8 capability, no StorageBuffer8BitAccess)
https://github.com/iree-org/iree (IREE SPIR-V codegen: OpTypeArray with OpConstant length for shared tiles)

OQ1_barrier_race_warning_vs_error.rationale: Cross-invocation aliasing through shared memory is undecidable in the general case (loops, divergent branches, inter-block accesses). The straight-line lint is best-effort and advisory. A hard error on the provable straight-line case would be premature: it would require a substantially larger dataflow analysis surface and could generate false positives for kernels that structure their barrier elsewhere in the same block. The correct escalation path is: advisory warning in M3.2 → opt-in strict mode (@strict enforcement) in a future milestone that narrows the scope to cases the analysis can prove. This is exactly how the SubgroupOpInDivergentContext warning was handled in M1.4.
OQ1_barrier_race_warning_vs_error.caveats: The pessimistic reviewer may reasonably push for hard-error in the provable single-basic-block case. If they do, the compromise is: hard error only when BOTH (a) the write and read are in the SAME basic block with no intervening barrier AND (b) the enclosing kernel has workgroup size > 1. This is decidable and catches the most common mistake.

OQ2_divergent_barrier.position: DEFER to after M3.2, as proposed
OQ2_divergent_barrier.rationale: The matmul and attention kernels in M3.2 keep all barriers in uniform control flow (the K-loop body is uniform; all workgroup invocations execute the same loop trip count). Adding a divergent-barrier check would require a minimal CFG divergence analysis (at least a 'barrier must not be inside an if-else without @uniform_branch on the condition' check), which is out of scope for this milestone. The design correctly notes the kernels avoid this hazard; DESIGN.md §3.1.14 documents the known hazard. Defer is the right call.
OQ2_divergent_barrier.caveats: None — this is the same deferral that has been in place since M1.4 and the matmul/attention control flow is explicitly uniform.

OQ3_max_shared_memory_ceiling.rationale: 65536 bytes is the VkPhysicalDeviceLimits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize value reported by desktop NVIDIA (48 KiB default, 100 KiB with VK_EXT_shader_subgroup_uniform_control_flow opt-in on Blackwell), AMD (64 KiB LDS on RDNA3), and Intel Arc (64 KiB EU-SLM). It is a safe, portable conservative ceiling that avoids driver crashes on any production desktop hardware. The 16384 portable-minimum warning is the right advisory for embedded/mobile targets. The @target-driven ceiling is the correct follow-on for Blackwell-specific kernels that could use the 99 KiB extended LDS. For M3.2's tile sizes (TILE_M=16, TILE_K=32, f16: 2*16*32*2=2048 bytes per shared array), we are well under any ceiling.
OQ3_max_shared_memory_ceiling.caveats: The NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell) maxComputeSharedMemorySize may report 49152 (48 KiB) by default without the opt-in. This does not affect M3.2 since the tile sizes are small.

OQ4_fa2_c1_c2_staging.rationale: C1 (non-streaming shared-tiled attention) genuinely exercises the full shared[T,N] tiling and barrier pipeline (K/V tiles staged into shared[f16], barrier before the softmax dot-product phase). AT-1606 is the load-bearing barrier test independently of FA2; AT-1630 is the C1 attention correctness gate. C1 is a meaningful, publishable result (it corresponds to 'naive tiled attention' in the FA2 paper, which outperforms the unfused baseline). C2 (streaming online softmax) is purely an algorithmic optimization on top of the same data movement — its bit-exactness against C1 via @equiv_fp_tol is the anti-reward-hacking discipline the project exists to enforce. Deferring C2 to M3.2b is the responsible choice given that C2's running-max/running-denominator arithmetic is a separate, high-risk correctness surface.
OQ4_fa2_c1_c2_staging.caveats: None. The staging is honest and the C2 deferral rationale (online-rescale verification surface, overrun risk, anti-reward-hacking baseline) is exactly correct.

OQ5_coopmat_load_from_shared_byte_identi.position: APPROVE discriminator approach, flag missing AT
OQ5_coopmat_load_from_shared_byte_identi.rationale: The CoopMatBuiltin::Load + CoopMatLoadSource::{Buffer, Shared} discriminator is additive: existing coopmat_load calls with a buffer arg default to Buffer, so the M2.1/M3.1 emit path is unchanged. The only risk is an unintended change to the existing buffer-source access-chain emission. This risk is mitigated by AT-1611 (all existing SPIR-V byte fixtures unchanged), but a named test specifically asserting that the q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc output is byte-identical to the M3.1.5 known-good fixture would close the loop. Recommend this be added as AT-1613 or noted as an amendment to AT-1611.
OQ5_coopmat_load_from_shared_byte_identi.caveats: If AT-1611 already covers q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc (which it should, since it says 'all existing SPIR-V byte-fixtures are UNCHANGED'), this concern is already addressed by the existing AT. The coder should confirm AT-1611's fixture list includes this file.

OQ6_hole_into_literal_n.position: APPROVE literal-only N in M3.2 via source-text substitution
OQ6_hole_into_literal_n.rationale: Requiring the autotuner to substitute the hole into a literal before the parser sees the source is a clean layering decision that preserves anti-pattern #1 (no inference) for the language grammar while making holes effective at the source-text level. The M2.3 hole-resolution path already does source-text substitution; this extends that behavior to shared array sizes. The ergonomic constraint ('a shared[f16, ?tile_k * 16] is not directly parseable') is real but acceptable for M3.2. Document it prominently in DESIGN.md §3.1.14 and in the @strategy annotation semantics so future agent authors know to use the autotuner's substitution, not a bare hole reference in the N position.

test_suggestions: Add AT-1613: assert that the existing q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc SPIR-V output is byte-identical before and after the CoopMatLoadSource discriminator is added to CoopMatBuiltin::Load. This ensures the additive discriminator (Buffer-source default) does not change the existing coopmat emission path. This is implied by AT-1611 but should be explicitly named to guard the M2.1 coopmat path.

AT-1606 should explicitly assert that the barrier-ABSENT variant emits the SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead warning (currently the design says 'documented as racy' but does not explicitly say the test ASSERTS the warning's presence). Recommend: the test fixture calls the compiler on the no-barrier variant and asserts the warning list contains SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead.

Consider adding a test (can be folded into AT-1607 or AT-1609) that asserts TWO distinct shared arrays of the SAME element type each have DISTINCT OpTypeArray and OpVariable ids but SHARE the same OpTypePointer Workgroup pointer type for the elem-ptr cache. This guards against the 'dedup must not collapse distinct arrays' edge case in the spec.

AT-1622 description is correct and sufficient for proving holes are non-inert. Consider also asserting that the K-loop trip count in the SPIR-V disassembly differs (e.g., the K-loop bound constant = total_K / tile_k, so tile_k=16 gives K/16 iterations, tile_k=32 gives K/32). This provides a second structural proof beyond the shared-array size check.

feasibility_assessment.part_a_shared_TN: HIGH — The SPIR-V emission pattern (OpTypeArray + OpTypePointer Workgroup + OpVariable Workgroup + OpAccessChain single-index) is straightforward rspirv builder calls. The HIR plumbing mirrors buffer.rs/buffers.rs which already has 14 passing tests. The barrier reuse is verbatim. Estimated implementation risk: LOW.
feasibility_assessment.part_b_competitive_matmul: MEDIUM-HIGH — The shared-staged + coopmat path requires extending CoopMatBuiltin::Load with the source discriminator, which touches the existing M2.1 HIR and codegen coopmat path. The risk is bounded by the additive default (Buffer-source unchanged) and the AT-1611/AT-1613 guards. The genuine-holes mechanism via source-text substitution is already proven in M2.3. Estimated implementation risk: MEDIUM (the coopmat extension is the riskiest piece).
feasibility_assessment.part_c1_attention: MEDIUM — The non-streaming shared-tiled attention is algorithmically straightforward (standard softmax over the K dimension, no online rescaling). The main risk is the CPU reference attention implementation in benches/common.rs — it must be correct for AT-1630 to be meaningful. The @equiv_fp_tol(1e-3) tolerance is generous enough to accommodate f16 accumulation errors. Estimated implementation risk: MEDIUM (CPU reference accuracy is the risk).
feasibility_assessment.overall_loe: The design estimates 4000-6000 LOC for the full milestone. This is plausible: PART A (shared[T,N] full pipeline) is ~1200-1500 LOC; PART B (matmul with coopmat extension) is ~1500-2000 LOC; PART C1 (attention + CPU reference) is ~800-1200 LOC; tests and benches are ~500-800 LOC. Total: 4000-5500 LOC, within the ROADMAP estimate.

goal_alignment: STRONG — M3.2 directly advances the thesis. shared[T,N] is the FG.6 language feature explicitly listed as a ROADMAP dependency for M3.2. The competitive matmul is the honest follow-on to M3.1.5's 'naive 3.6% of cuBLAS' finding. The FA2 C1 staging delivers a publishable attention baseline without overrunning scope. The milestone advances FG.6 (shared memory), advances the ≥80%-of-FA3 aspiration (via C2's deferred streaming optimization), and produces the first TFLOPS-competitive matmul number for the project.

summary: The M3.2 design is sound, feasible, and appropriately scoped. The shared[T,N] language feature is the correct SPIR-V design (OpTypeArray + OpTypePointer Workgroup + global OpVariable + single-index access chain, no new capability), correctly distinguished from the SSBO two-index pattern, and correctly relying on the existing workgroup_barrier() verbatim for cross-invocation visibility — all three of which are confirmed against the SPIR-V unified spec, SPV_KHR_8bit_storage spec, and the existing codebase. The M3.1.5 inert-holes lesson is explicitly addressed with a structural non-inertness test (AT-1622). The FA2 staging (C1 correctness-first non-streaming attention lands; C2 streaming online softmax defers) is honest, well-reasoned, and mirrors the FlashAttention-2 paper's own decomposition. The test suite AT-1600..1632 covers the full pipeline (lex → GPU dispatch → runtime preflight), includes the barrier-visibility oracle (AT-1606) as the load-bearing correctness test, and satisfies anti-pattern #9. The four minor concerns are all non-blocking: the CoopMatBuiltin::Load byte-identity test gap should be addressed by adding AT-1613; the barrier-absent warning assertion in AT-1606 should be explicit; the shared-array dedup edge case is worth a targeted test. None of these require a redesign. The open questions are correctly resolved by the Architect: warning-only barrier-race lint, divergent barrier deferred, 65536-byte static ceiling, FA2 staged, coopmat discriminator additive. APPROVE for Pessimistic Design Reviewer and Coder phases.
